content.title: Definition of HONOR
content.text: 1 b : respect that is given to someone who is admired : recognition brought honor to the school c(1) : high moral standards of behavior : integrity lived by a strict code of honor (2) : someone's word given as a guarantee of performance On my honor, I will be there. 2 : something (such as an opportunity) that gives someone a sense of pride : privilege had the honor of informing her that she'd won the scholarship granted the honor of christening the ship It was an honor to be invited. 3 : a person of superior standing —now used especially as a title for a holder of high officeif Your Honor please 4 : one whose worth brings respect or fame : credit an honor to the profession 5 : an indication or symbol of distinction: such as a : an exalted title or rank received the honor of emeritus upon retiring b(1) : badge, decoration the nation's highest civilian honor, the Presidential Medal of Freedom (2) : a ceremonial rite or observance buried with full military honors c : an award in a contest or field of competition Her debut novel won a number of honors in its first year. e honors plural (1) : an academic distinction conferred on a student who has successfully done work at a high level (2)honors plural but singular in construction : a special high-level course of study for students supplementing or replacing a regular course —usually used before another nountaking honors math and honors French 6 old-fashioned : chastity, purity "You've compromised your honor with a man who lives in my house. Of course this has upset me!"— Kaitlyn Greenidge 7 honors plural : social courtesies or civilities extended by a host asked her to do the honors 8 a(1) : an ace, king, queen, jack, or ten especially of the trump suit in bridge (2) : the scoring value of honors held in bridge —usually used in plural b : the privilege of playing first from the tee in golf 9 : the center point of the upper half of an armorial escutcheon transitive verb 1 a : to regard or treat (someone) with admiration and respect : to regard or treat with honor raised to honor their parents a promise to love and honor each other in marriage honored us with her presence b : to give special recognition to : to confer honor on honored as player of the year a dinner honoring the library's centennial 2 a : to live up to or fulfill the terms of honor a commitment/contract/warranty 3 : to salute with a bow in square dancing Synonyms of honor Choose the Right Synonym for honor honor, homage, reverence, deference mean respect and esteem shown to another. honor may apply to the recognition of one's right to great respect or to any expression of such recognition. the nomination is an honor homage adds the implication of accompanying praise. paying homage to Shakespeare reverence implies profound respect mingled with love, devotion, or awe. great reverence for my father deference implies a yielding or submitting to another's judgment or preference out of respect or reverence. showed no deference to their elders synonyms see in addition honesty Examples of honor in a Sentence Noun Many of the Persians, despite belonging to the Barbarian Other, come off with honor and dignity in his pages, even during the final narrative of Xerxes' invasion. — Peter Green, New York Review of Books, 15 May 2008 Whoever footed the bill, the episode gave Marsh a taste of the grand life she yearned for. Presiding at balls in her honor and making entrances at lavish picnics were distinctions she could never have dreamed of back home. — Edmund S. Morgan et al., New York Review of Books, 27 Sept. 2007 "As I was saying," he said, smiling at the sea of students before him, all of whom were still gazing transfixed at Mad-Eye Moody, "we are to have the honor of hosting a very exciting event over the coming months, an event that has not been held for over a century." — J.
